Topic T1 · First Impression

What You’d Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item F2 is a long, plain titanium socket cap screw: a silver, uncoated bolt with a cylindrical head, an internal hex drive and a coarse thread. Every one of those features is encoded in the part number.

As received: no finish, a cylindrical socket cap head, and a coarse thread along the end of the shank. The grid mat and 10–40 mm scale show the true size.

Topic T3 · Measurement System & Standard

Metric, Built to DIN 912

The metric system measures bolts in millimeters and is the most widely used system in industry. Here is the whole item in one reference table.

How a Metric Screw Is Named

Nomenclature

A metric screw is written as M followed by a number: the outside diameter of the screw in millimeters. Here, M10 means 10 mm.

Three Measurements

In the metric system a screw is described by its diameter, its length and its thread pitch — all in millimeters.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

Titanium

The part is made of titanium: a lustrous, silvery metal with high strength and corrosion resistance.

Titanium metal: silvery and lustrous.
Titanium sits on the periodic table as Ti, atomic number 22.

Properties

Lustrous, silver-colored, with high strength and corrosion resistance.

Where It Comes From

Titanium is found combined in practically all rocks, sand, clay and other soils.

On the Periodic Table

Symbol Ti, atomic number 22.

Why It Matters

Strength plus corrosion resistance is why titanium fasteners are specified for demanding jobs — see .

Titanium comes in several grades — see for which one this part uses.

Topic T5 · Grade

Grade 5 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V)

The “G5” in the description calls out grade 5: an alloy of titanium, aluminum and vanadium, with properties of strength, ductility, toughness and formability.

Requirement

M10-1.5 X 50 SOCKET CAP G5 TITANIUM · Grade 5 titanium per ASTM B348.

The Governing Standard: ASTM B348
Click any image to enlarge.
ASTM B348 describes the elements, and the quantity and percentage of each, that grade 5 material must contain. Grade 5 is highlighted in both tables.

Chemistry (Table 1)

Grade 5 is UNS R56400: about 5.5–6.75% aluminum and 3.5–4.5% vanadium, with limits on carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and iron.

Strength (Table 2)

Grade 5 minimum tensile strength is 130 ksi (895 MPa), with a 120 ksi (828 MPa) yield strength.

Why We Always Ask for Certificates

A Customer Requirement

When a PPAP is made, we always ask for documents such as material certificates.

What They Prove

The certificate lists the chemical properties in the material, so we can be sure our supplier is sending us the material described.

Grade 5 titanium bar stock (reference photo).

Topic T6 · Finish

Plain: Just the Material

This part has no finish. It is only the material, so the finish is called out as plain.

The finished part: bare titanium, nothing plated or coated on top.

Requirement

Finish: Plain — no plating, coating or treatment.

What You See

The natural silver-grey of the titanium itself, on the head, shank and thread.

Why It Works

Titanium already brings its own corrosion resistance (see Topic T4), so there is nothing a coating would need to add.

Topic T7 · Thread Type

A Coarse Thread

We identify the thread type from the thread pitch. This part has a pitch of 1.5 mm, which the thread pitch chart (from the Fastener Black Book) lists as coarse for M10.

Coarse vs. fine: a coarse thread has fewer threads over the same length, so you can see the difference by eye.
Thread pitch identification chart: the M10 row shows 1.5 in the Coarse column (fine would be 1.25).
Spotting It on the Part
The threaded section of the part, outlined in green.

Requirement

Thread type: Coarse.

How to Tell

Look at the thread pitch: 1.5 mm is the standard coarse pitch for M10.

Next: the thread itself and how it is checked, in .

Topic T8 · Thread & Thread Pitch

M10-1.5: Diameter and Pitch

An M10 screw has an outside diameter of 10 mm. If the screw has a thread pitch, a second number is added after the M — so M10 x 1.50 means a 10 mm screw with a 1.50 mm thread pitch.

The threaded length on the DIN 912 drawing.
The same threaded section on the real part.
Checking the Thread: Ring Gauge
A GO ring gauge for M10 x 1.5 — the part must thread into it.

Measuring the Thread

The way to measure these threads is with ring gauges. The gauge is marked with the thread size (M10x1.5) and its tolerance class (6g).

Checking the Pitch: Thread Pitch Gauge
Thread pitch: the distance from one thread crest to the next — 1.5 mm.
Reading the pitch with a thread pitch gauge: the 1.50 blade fits the thread.

This part has a 1.5 mm pitch, and the gauge lets you verify it quickly. On to the next dimension: .

Topic T9 · Length

50 mm Overall

The description calls out a 50 mm length. In DIN 912 the letter l is the length, with tolerances of 49.5 mm minimum and 50.5 mm maximum.

The length l on the drawing (green box, left) and the nominal-length 50 row of the table (green box, right): 49.5 min, 50.5 max.
Measuring It on the Part
Length is measured from under the head to the end of the screw.
A caliper measures the length directly.

Nominal

50 mm.

Tolerance

49.5 mm min – 50.5 mm max.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term’s “jump” button to see it in context.

ASTM B348

The ASTM standard specification for titanium and titanium alloy bars and billets. It lists the elements, and the amount of each, that a grade such as grade 5 must contain.

Caliper

A hand-held measuring tool used to check length, head diameter, head height and socket size on this part.

Coarse Thread

A thread with a larger pitch (fewer threads over the same length) than a fine thread. For M10, the coarse pitch is 1.5 mm.

DIN 912 / ISO 4762

The German and international standards that define hex socket head cap screws — the head shape, drive, dimensions and tolerances this part is built to.

Grade 5 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V)

An alloy of titanium, aluminum and vanadium with a balance of strength, ductility, toughness and formability.

Hex Socket

A hexagonal recess in the head, driven with a hex key. The drive of this part.

M10-1.5

The metric thread callout: a 10 mm outside diameter with a 1.5 mm thread pitch.

Material Certificate

A supplier document that shows the chemical properties of the material, confirming it is what was described. Requested with every PPAP.

Metric System

The measuring system for bolts based on millimeters, the most widely used in industry.

PPAP

Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package, including material certificates, that a supplier submits to prove it can make a part to print.

Ring Gauge

A ring with an internal thread of the exact size and tolerance, used to check external threads.

Socket Cap

A cylindrical head with an internal hexagon. The head style of this part.

Thread Pitch

The distance between one thread and the next. For this part it is 1.5 mm.

Thread Pitch Gauge

A set of thin blades, each cut to a specific pitch, used to check a screw’s thread pitch.

Titanium

A lustrous, silver-colored metal with high strength and corrosion resistance. Symbol Ti, atomic number 22.

VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts at the customer’s location. This module is named after Item F2’s cell on the VMI bin card.
